A month is enough for rows 98 to 102 if they are done deliberately and in that order — **the locked parish transcripts first, because they are the only thing here that cannot be got anywhere else.** Worth agreeing a date to review what is left, rather than discovering the end of it the same way as last time. **UPDATED 16 SEPTEMBER: rows 98 to 102 are all done, on the first day.** The subscription has been worked out rather than used up, and the honest summary is that **Findmypast had less for this family than the work list expected, and gave it up quickly.** **What it delivered:** Sebastiano Mazza on the 1959 roll at Wacol; the Crupi brothers at Tully; Rocco Arena's absence from the American census proved across the whole country; the parish transcripts opened and audited. **What it turned out not to hold:** Queensland rolls after 1959, any Australian arrival the free NAA index does not already have, any New York burial, and any godparent. **So the question is no longer «what else can we get before it expires» — it is whether the month is worth renewing at all.** On this evidence, no: the open work now points at **Ancestry or the NLA** for the post-1959 rolls (row 104), **the NAA** for naturalisations and one manifest image (rows 105, 110, 112), and **free New York city records** (row 113). **The one thing still unmined here is the Victorian passenger lists** (row 111). Worth a decision, not a diary date.

rows.what: The Queensland rolls after 1959 — which means the NLA or Ancestry, not Findmypast
rows.note: **Row 99 hit a wall that a subscription cannot climb.** Findmypast's last Queensland electoral roll is **1959**. Sebastiano Mazza is on it at Wacol; **Domenica Prostamo is not on it at all**, under either name — most likely because she had not yet been naturalised, since her husband would have been naturalised first. **Every year that would settle that is outside this collection.** The near-annual Queensland run to 1980 is held by the **National Library of Australia** and by **Ancestry**, and it would follow this household through Wacol year by year, catch Domenica's first enrolment, and place Frank Mazza as he came of age. **This is David's call, not the archive's** — it is a second paid service, and the Findmypast month is already running.

rows.what: Sebastiano Mazza's naturalisation, which the 1959 roll proves exists
rows.note: **An enrolment is a proof of citizenship, and that is the quiet finding in row 99.** Only British subjects could be enrolled to vote, so Sebastiano Mazza's presence on the 1959 Queensland roll means **he was naturalised between his arrival in 1949 and 1959**, and a naturalisation file exists for him. **The NAA holds them** — series A712, A714 and the certificate registers — and this archive already knows how to work the NAA index from the passenger work. The file would give his **birth date, his birthplace, his occupation, his address, and often the ship and date he arrived**, which would corroborate the crossing independently. **And it should be run for Domenica Prostamo at the same time**, because her naturalisation date is exactly what would explain her absence from the 1959 roll. **DONE 16 SEPTEMBER — the file exists and it is cited.** **NAA: J25, 1971/1074, «Mazza, Sebastiano; wife Domenica [nee Prostamo]», Brisbane, 1950–1971.** It names both of them and her maiden name, and its date range covers their whole Australian lives to 1971. **It is paper, it is not digitised, and it is «not yet examined»** — so it needs an access examination request before anyone can read it. That is row 115, and it is not this archive's to make. **It may also settle row 21**: a Queensland immigration file opening in 1950 should record how and when Domenica came.

rows.what: Andrea Mazza, timber cutter at Tully in 1959 — a lead a roll cannot settle
rows.note: **Tully is not a coincidence and it is not yet a relative.** Rosario Mazza's daughter **Carmela Mazza was born at Tully in 1926**, so this family had a household in that exact sub-district; and the 1959 roll puts an **ANDREA MAZZA, timber cutter, at Cardwell in the Tully sub-district**. No Andrea appears anywhere in the tree as it stands. **A roll carries no parents and no birth year, so it cannot decide him.** What could: the Queensland BDM birth index for Tully in the 1920s and 1930s, which *is* inside its window and would name his parents; or Michael, if the family remembers a branch that stayed north. Left as a lead rather than attached — the archive has been offered two Arena namesakes in New York this week and excluded both on a parent's name.

rows.what: Never record a negative from an untested search parameter — the rule this sweep nearly broke
rows.note: **Raised and closed the same day, because it nearly put a falsehood in the record.** On Findmypast's results URL a wrong parameter fails in **two different ways and neither announces itself**. `state=Queensland` and `page=2` render a filter chip and report **«0 results found»** — word for word what a genuine negative looks like. `street=progress road` is **discarded in silence** and the unfiltered count comes back unchanged, so the search you think you ran is not the one that ran. The first was caught only because the *unfiltered* search plainly listed Queensland rows. **The rule now in the log: control-test a parameter against a search known to return rows before believing any zero it produces.** This is the same family of trap as `fathersfirstname` for `fatherfirstname` earlier in this work, and as the multi-comune trap in the Antenati registers — *the instrument answering a different question than the one asked.* Written up in [what has been searched](/searched/).

rows.what: Donato and Nicotra in Queensland — two clusters off this family's own spine, unopened
rows.note: **The electoral sweep walked into two surnames nobody here has looked for in Australia.** **DONATO: 65 rows**, and the Queensland block holds a **CANDELORE DONATO enrolled in 1941 and 1949**, a **CANDO DONATO** in 1939 and 1959, and a **DOMENICO DONATO** in 1959. **CANDELORO DONATO IS ONE OF THE FOUR WALLS** — born about 1783 at Scilla, the point where [the Donato quarter](/lines/) stops. He is plainly not the same man, and *that is the interest*: southern Italian families name a grandson for his grandfather, so a Candeloro Donato in Queensland is what a **descendant of the wall** looks like from this end. Domenico Donato is the name on the 1816 birth act that came out of the Scilla processetti this week. **NICOTRA: 39 rows**, almost all Queensland, a family enrolled continuously from 1934 to 1959 — **Filippo, Gregorio, Giuseppe, Carmela, Leonarda, Leonard**. **Nicotra is Sebastiano Mazza's mother's name**, Maria Concetta Nicotra. **Neither is claimed and neither can be, from rolls alone** — no parents, no birth years. The route that could decide them is the Queensland BDM birth and marriage indexes, which *are* inside their windows for the 1930s and 1940s and do carry parents.

rows.what: Which Antonio Crupi died in 1982 — two men of that name in north Queensland
rows.note: **A small ambiguity, written down so it is not quietly resolved the wrong way later.** The 1959 roll holds **two Antonio Crupi**: a **cane farmer at Dean Street, Tully**, and a **farmer at Silkwood East in the Innisfail sub-district**. Angela Crupi's brother **ANTONINO CRUPI died 15 April 1982** (reg 1982/52783), son of Francesco Crupi and Maria Vecchio. **A roll cannot tell which man he is** — it carries no parents and no birth year. The Tully one is the better bet only because his brothers Pietro and Mario are both at Tully, and *better bet* is not evidence. **What would settle it:** the 1982 death registration's district, or the marriage of an Antonino Crupi registered 24 August 1940 (1940/C/3314), which would name a wife to match against **Nellie Crupi**, the woman sharing Dean Street with the Tully man.

rows.what: The original Ugolino Vivaldi manifest at the NAA — free, and the only thing that can settle Domenica's crossing
rows.note: **Row 100 proved the subscription cannot do this and pointed at what can.** Domenica Prostamo's 1951 crossing is graded **candidate** on a good argument — right month, right year, right port, right married surname, and «Domenico» one letter from Domenica. **What it lacks is an age or a sex**, and the index line has neither, on Findmypast or at the NAA. **The manifest image does.** RecordSearch serves barcode **30133197** as a scanned page, free, and the handwritten entry would give the age and sex outright — and show **everyone else on that page**, which is how a two-year-old Salvatore Mazza would appear, since infants are not separately indexed. **This is the single cheapest upgrade available to this archive**: one image, no subscription, and it converts a candidate into a documented crossing or kills it. **DONE 16 SEPTEMBER — and it killed the candidate rather than confirming it.** This row said the image would «convert a candidate into a documented crossing or kill it». It killed it. The master list of trip 2/51 carries **one Mazza**, no. 476, bound for **Narracan, Victoria**. There is **no Prostamo aboard** under any spelling, and **no second Mazza**, though the list names children individually — so no two-year-old Salvatore. **And the port column settles it**: unlabelled, but every `-F-` passenger appears in the Department of Immigration's separate *Schedule of Alien Passengers for debarkation at Fremantle*, one for one. MAZZA Domenico is `-M-`, and he is **absent from that schedule**, which runs MARTINELLI straight to MERENDINO. **Domenica Prostamo was going to her husband in Brisbane; this man landed at Melbourne for a Gippsland shire.** Retracted in [the corrections](/corrections/), regraded *flagged*, and the two voyage rows are off [the crossings](/crossings/). **Her March 1951 crossing is unknown again — see row 21.**

rows.what: The Victorian passenger lists 1852–1923 — the part of the subscription that is genuinely not the NAA
rows.note: **Found by accident while proving row 100 a dead end.** «Australia, Inward, Outward & Coastal Passenger Lists 1826-1972» is two different things stitched together. The post-1945 half is the NAA index re-served. **The pre-1940 half is not**: ids of the form ANZ/VCPL and ANZ/MIGR/VICTORIAPASSLIST are the **Victorian inward, outward and coastal lists**, which the NAA index does not hold. The Mazza search returns rows there from **1891, 1896, 1897, 1898, 1900, 1901, 1910, 1911, 1914 and 1919**. **Why it might matter:** this archive's Australian story starts in 1925 with Michele Mazza on the *Palermo*, and everything before that is assumed to be Italy. **These lists cover the years when it might not have been.** Sicilian and Calabrian men worked passages to Victoria and went home again, and a Mazza or a Prostamo on an **outward** list would be exactly that. Speculative, cheap to test, and nobody has looked. **DONE 16 SEPTEMBER, and the guess was wrong for reasons worth writing down.** The Victorian material is mostly **coastal** — Strahan to Melbourne, Fremantle to Melbourne — which is people already in Australia moving around it, not people arriving from Italy. **And the coastal rows are mostly nameless**, carrying a surname, a sex and an age and no given name, so a real ancestor there could not be recognised anyway. The named overseas Victorian rows are **British subjects**. **The control makes it a negative rather than a shrug:** searched by name, Michele Mazza's 1925 crossing from Messina to Brisbane comes straight back. The collection can see this family when it is there. Before 1925 it is not. **The Australian story still starts where this archive has always said it starts.**

rows.what: Rocco Arena's naturalisation is a pre-1906 New York court filing — which no subscription holds
rows.note: **Row 101 could not find the papers and instead worked out when they must have been filed.** He is in America from 1892, he is in the 1900 census, he is **gone from the whole country by 1910**, and he sails in 1913 as a **US citizen**. So the declaration and petition were filed in New York **between 1892 and about 1906**. **That is exactly why Findmypast cannot see him**: its United States Naturalization Petitions collection begins after the 1906 standardisation, and before 1906 these cases were heard in **state, county and city courts** as well as federal ones. **The finding aid is a NARA index to petitions filed in New York City courts, 1792–1906** — on microfilm, held by the National Archives at New York City, and on no subscription site. *(The series number should be confirmed before anyone writes to them; it is believed to be M1674.)* **What has changed is the size of the problem**: the search is now bounded to a fourteen-year window in one city, instead of a lifetime in a country.

rows.what: The first Antonio Arena's death, 1896×1902 — free records, and neither has been tried
rows.note: **An inference this archive has published, and the record that would settle it is free.** Rocco Arena's first son **Antonio was born 3 October 1896**; a **second Antonio was born 13 October 1902**. This archive reads that as the first boy dying in between — the same reading it makes of [Orazio Arena's two sons named Domenico](/scilla/) at Scilla. **It is sound and it is still an inference.** **Findmypast cannot test it**: there is no New York Roman Catholic burials collection — baptisms and marriages only, and «Congregational Records» is empty even of Russo. **Two places can.** The **New York City death certificates** at the Municipal Archives are indexed from 1862 and searchable for nothing; and the interment registers of **Calvary Cemetery**, where the Italian Catholic dead of lower Manhattan were mostly buried. A death between 1896 and 1902 for an infant of 141 or 198 Mulberry Street is a narrow, well-specified search. **It would also date the family's last years in America**, which matters now that the census says they were gone by 1910.

rows.what: Salvatore Mazza's arrival, which fell with his mother's
rows.note: **Collateral damage from row 110, and it should not be left implicit.** This archive placed **Salvatore Mazza (b. 1948)** on the *Ugolino Vivaldi* at `inferred`, on the reasoning that infants are not separately indexed and he belonged on his mother's voyage. **The reasoning was fine and the voyage was wrong.** Reading the manifest also removed its own premise: **this master list names children individually** — the Mellino family of eight, the Puusaari of six, a Campagna aged 1 — so an infant *would* have been listed. **He has no documented crossing now.** The tree records a Fremantle arrival out of Genoa with no date; that, and the family account of a son not yet three, are all that remain. He travels with whatever voyage row 21 eventually finds for his mother.

rows.what: Ask the NAA to examine J25 1971/1074 — the family's own naturalisation file
rows.note: **The single best unread document about Michael's grandparents, and getting at it is a form, not research.** **NAA: J25, 1971/1074, «Mazza, Sebastiano; wife Domenica [nee Prostamo]»**, Brisbane, contents 1950–1971. Its access status is **«not yet examined»**, which means nobody has ever asked for it. **Anyone can ask, it costs nothing, and the NAA then examines it for release** — the usual wait is about ninety days. **Why it is worth the form:** a Queensland immigration and naturalisation file covering 1950 to 1971 would carry Sebastiano's naturalisation, his address history, his occupation, and — since she is named on it — **how and when Domenica actually arrived**, which [row 21](/worklist/) badly needs now that the Ugolino Vivaldi is disproved. **This archive cannot lodge the request**; it needs a person with an account and a postal address. Michael is in Brisbane, where the file is.

rows.what: Carmela Mazza cannot have been born at Tully in 1926
rows.note: **A contradiction found by accident, and it broke one of my own arguments the same day.** The tree has **Carmela Mazza born 1926 at Tully, Queensland**. But **NAA: A12508, 31/1454** has her arriving at Brisbane on **7 December 1937** aboard the *Viminale*, **aged eight, as an Italian alien**, with her mother Angela Crupi and her sister Maria. **A child born at Tully in 1926 would be eleven and an Australian-born British subject**, needing no alien declaration at all. **The record is not loose about ages** — Maria's «age 15» matches the tree's 1922 exactly. **So she was born in Italy about 1929.** **What it cost:** I had argued that the Tully timber cutter of 1959 ([row 106](/worklist/)) was interesting because a Mazza household already stood at Tully in 1926. On this evidence it did not. The Tully connection survives, but through **the Crupi brothers**, not through a birth that did not happen. **What would settle it:** the Queensland BDM birth index, which covers 1926 and would simply show whether a Carmela Mazza was registered at Tully at all.

rows.what: The rest of the NAA aliens cards — Crupi, Arena, Polistena, and the other two brothers
rows.note: **Row 50 found the seam and did not empty it.** Mario Crupi's card (D4028) turned out to be **digitised, free, and the richest document this archive holds on anyone in Australia** — birth date, birthplace, occupation, arrival, a physical description, and an internment camp. **There should be more.** **Wanted:** cards for **PIETRO** and **ANTONINO CRUPI**, the other two brothers, both of whom are on the Queensland electoral rolls; for **ROSARIO MAZZA**, to set against his internment dossier; and for **ROCCO ARENA** and the **POLISTENA**, who arrived in 1949 and may be too late for the wartime series. **Note the series split:** D4028 is Queensland aliens registration; B78 and BP25/1 and SP908/1 are the Victorian, Queensland and New South Wales equivalents, and a family scattered across states will be scattered across series. **Search by surname in all record categories, then check each item for «View digital copy»** — that is what separates an hour's work from a request form.

rows.what: Rocco Arena married his first cousin — and one act away from proving it
rows.note: **A question this archive asked itself and left open has almost certainly been answered.** The row for **ANNA ARLOTTA**, Generosa Costa's mother, noted that Rocco Arena's mother was **Serafina ARLOTTA** and his wife's mother was **Anna ARLOTTA**, and said in as many words that whether they were sisters *had not been tested*. **The Scilla death index tests it.** Anna Arlotta, died 16 March 1915, is «Padre GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, Madre MARIA COSTA, Coniuge ANTONINO COSTA» — and Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa are **Serafina Arlotta's own parents**. Her husband's name matches the Antonio Costa the 1888 marriage act gives as Generosa's father. **So the two women were sisters and Rocco Arena and Generosa Costa were first cousins.** **Graded *probable*, not *certain*, and deliberately.** Arlotta and Costa are both common at Scilla and nothing read so far rules out a second Anna Arlotta married to a second Antonino Costa. **One act settles it**: the 1915 death act itself, which gives her age and parents in full, or Generosa Costa's own birth act. Both are inside the surviving run.

rows.what: Does Antenati's name index cover BIRTHS and MARRIAGES too, or only deaths?
rows.note: **The single highest-value question in the work list, because the answer re-prices a dozen rows.** Today's sweep queried `/search-nominative/?cognome=X&localita=Scilla` and every result came back an **atto di morte**, 1910–1943. **That may be all Scilla has indexed, or it may be all that these four surnames happened to return.** Not the same thing, and the difference is enormous: if **marriages** are indexed, [row 71](/worklist/) — Nunziata Donato × Giovanni Polistena, about 1916 — is answered by a query. If **births** are, so is Camillo Antonio Polistena's birth act and half of [row 4](/worklist/). **Test it properly:** query a surname with no locality and read the *tipologia* facet, which will say what act types exist and how many of each.

rows.what: Run the name index for the rest of the Scilla surnames
rows.note: **Four surnames were swept today and there are at least eight more on the spine.** Wanted: **COSTA** (which should hold Generosa), **SOFI**, **ZIRILLI**, **MARTELLO**, **RUSSO**, **PALADINO**, **ROMANO** and **PONTILLO** — the last two because [row 41](/worklist/) has just been resolved *against* the tree, and the index is where a Romano family behind Giovanna would show up if one exists. **Cheap and mechanical**, one paced fetch each, and every act carries father, mother and spouse.

rows.what: Generosa Costa's death — absent from the Arena index, so look under Costa
rows.note: **Her husband's death act of 1932 names her as his wife, so she was alive or recently dead in February 1932.** She does not appear as *the deceased* anywhere in the Arena results, which is expected — she would be indexed under **COSTA**. Worth doing on its own because she is the last of the New York household whose end is unknown: Rocco died in 1932, their daughter Serafina in 1912, and the two Antonios and Clementina have no recorded end at all.

rows.what: Read the four acts the index only summarises
rows.note: **An index line is not an act — this archive says so about NAA item titles and the same rule applies here.** Four acts are now identified and none has been opened: **Rocco Arena, 8 February 1932**; **Giovanni Arena, 31 March 1936**; **Michele Donato, 10 May 1936**; **Camillo Antonio Polistena, 19 October 1924**. Each would give an **age** — which dates a birth — plus an address, a trade, and the two declarants. **Camillo Antonio's is the most valuable**: his age would date the birth this archive has only as «about 1835».

rows.what: Serafina Arena's death act, 1912 — does it record that she was born in America?
rows.note: **A small question with a large answer if it goes the right way.** She was baptised at Our Lady of Loretto, Manhattan, on 15 August 1898 and died at Scilla on 15 August 1912. **If the Scilla act names her birthplace as New York, that is the return migration written down in an Italian register** — the only document here that would state it outright rather than by inference from three absences. If it simply says Scilla, that is worth knowing too, because the index's «Nascita: Scilla» field may be a default rather than a claim.

rows.what: Domenico and Anna Arlotta died two days apart — read both acts
rows.note: **14 and 16 March 1915, brother and sister, both children of Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa.** Two deaths in one family in one week is not ordinary and the acts will say why: an epidemic, a fire, or a boat. **Scilla is a fishing town** and the sea takes siblings together. Whatever the cause, both acts carry ages, which would date Serafina Arlotta's siblings and bracket the marriage [row 39](/worklist/) wants.

rows.what: Settle whether Rocco Arena married his first cousin — one act
rows.note: **[Row 118](/worklist/) grades it *probable*; this is the act that would make it *certain*.** Either **Anna Arlotta's death act of 16 March 1915**, which gives her age and parents in full, or **Generosa Costa's own birth act**, which would name her mother with a patronymic. **Both are inside the surviving run.** What is being ruled out is a second Anna Arlotta married to a second Antonino Costa — unlikely, and *unlikely* is not *ruled out*.

rows.what: Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta — thirteen years, and the arks are in hand
rows.note: **[Row 69](/worklist/) narrowed from forty-seven unread years to thirteen; this is the sweep itself.** They are named repeatedly as parents in the 1910–1943 index and never once as the deceased, and the annual index for 1889–1896 was read without them. **So they died between 1897 and 1909.** The Morti arks for every one of those years are now in `scilla-arks-italiano.tsv`. **Note the hole:** Antenati has no volume for **1909**, so twelve years are readable and one is not — [row 129](/worklist/).

rows.what: The two Scilla death volumes Antenati does not hold — 1888 and 1909
rows.note: **Found by listing the series rather than by failing to find someone in it, which is the better way round.** The Morti run is complete from 1866 to 1943 **except for 1888 and 1909** — and 1909 sits inside the thirteen-year window where Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta must have died. **This is the same shape as the Zambrone gap**: a hole in the digitisation, not necessarily in the record. **The second copy is the route** — these registers were kept in duplicate, one at the comune and one at the Tribunale, and it is the Tribunale copy Antenati filmed. Belongs with [row 9](/worklist/).

rows.what: List the Scilla death series BEFORE 1866 — rows 68 and 85 cannot start without it
rows.note: **`scilla-arks.tsv` holds 55 Nati and 54 Matrimoni volumes for 1816–1865 and NOT ONE Morti volume.** The restaurazione death series has never been listed, and two rows depend on it entirely: **[row 68](/worklist/)**, Filippo Arena and Domenica Costa, who died most likely in the 1850s–70s, and **[row 85](/worklist/)**, Domenico Arlotta, dead before April 1854. **One page load does it** — the same `s_size=100` trick that returned all 81 post-1866 volumes this afternoon. **Do it before either row is attempted**, for the reason [row 17](/worklist/) gives about mapping before sweeping.

rows.what: Orazio Arena married twice — Mariantonia Musolino
rows.note: **A whole second marriage, found as a by-product.** The Scilla death index gives Orazio Arena four children by **Giovanna Zirilli** — Teresa (d. 1913), Giuseppe (d. 1922), Maria Annunziata (d. 1933) and Alessandro Antonio (d. 1936) — and a fifth, **DOMENICO ARENA (d. 30 December 1923), whose mother is MARIANTONIA MUSOLINO**. **Musolino is a name this archive has never held.** Either Orazio married twice or there are two Orazio Arenas at Scilla — and this archive already knows this man had *two sons both named Domenico*, which is exactly the situation where a second wife gets overlooked. The marriage act would settle it.

rows.what: Two Antonio Arenas at Scilla, and both their wives are called Serafina
rows.note: **A collision to guard before it does damage, in the spirit of [row 97](/worklist/).** This family's **FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA** married **SERAFINA ARLOTTA**, and the index renders him simply «Antonio» on his sons' death acts. **But the same index holds an ANTONIO ARENA married to a SERAFINA DE LUCA** — parents of Grazia (d. 1913), Anna (d. 1917) and Annunziata (d. 1919). **Same given name, same wife's given name, same town, same decades.** Anyone sweeping «Antonio Arena + Serafina» will merge two families. **The mother's surname is the discriminator and it must be checked every time** — which is exactly how two Arena namesakes were excluded in New York this week.

rows.what: PIEDIMONTE ETNEO — is it name-indexed? The Crupi are from there too
rows.note: **The NAA card gave Mario Crupi's birth as 28 November 1905 at Piedimonte, province of Catania — the Mazza's own town.** So the Crupi and the Mazza came from one village, and **Angela Crupi's birth of 20 December 1900** with her parents **Francesco Crupi and Maria Vecchio** should be reachable in the registers the Mazza line already uses. **First test whether Piedimonte Etneo is in the name index at all** — if it is, two birth acts and a set of parents come back for two queries. If it is not, the acts are still there to be read by volume, **with exact dates in hand**, which is the cheapest register work there is.

rows.what: Are Briatico, Zambrone and Pizzo name-indexed?
rows.note: **The Calabrian half of this family has been worked entirely by volume-reading, and it may not have needed to be.** Scilla turned out to be name-indexed for deaths 1910–1943; nobody has checked whether **Briatico**, **Zambrone**, **Pizzo** or **San Costantino** are. **If any is, several open rows collapse into queries** — [row 84](/worklist/) (Caterina Cichello's death), [row 44](/worklist/) (the Melluso), [row 66](/worklist/) (Maria Fragalà's death at Pizzo). **One paced fetch per comune answers it.** Do it before any further Calabrian volume sweep.

rows.what: Build the name-index coverage map: comune × act type × years
rows.note: **The same argument as [row 17](/worklist/), one level up, and it will pay better.** Row 17 wants to know which Scilla volumes carry an annual index; **this wants to know which comuni and which years Antenati has indexed by name at all** — because where it has, the volume index does not matter. **Today's work was done blind**: the coverage was discovered by querying four surnames and noticing every hit was a death between 1910 and 1943. **One table, built once**, and every later question becomes «is it indexed» before «which volume».

rows.what: The Loveday records — Mario Crupi's internment, from the camp's own side
rows.note: **His aliens card says «18.8.42 LOVEDAY INTERNMENT CAMP / 30/12/43 Released and entrained for Brisbane» and that is all it says.** The NAA holds the camp's own series — nominal rolls, internee service and casualty forms, and the objection and appeal files that record **why** a man was interned. **The why is the part worth having**: north Queensland Italians were interned on the word of neighbours, and the files carry the allegation and sometimes the appeal. **Rosario Mazza's dossier (MP1103/1 Q8110) should be worked the same way**, and [row 7](/worklist/)'s Trove search now has two names and two dates to search on.

rows.what: The Scilla birth act of Camillo Antonio Polistena, about 1835
rows.note: **[Row 96](/worklist/) closed on his death act, which gave his parents. His birth act would give the arithmetic a check and the parents a second witness.** Scilla's births begin in 1816, so a birth about 1835 is inside the run. **What makes it worth doing now rather than before:** we know the parents to look for — **Giuseppe Polistena and Anna Pontillo** — so the read is a confirmation with a known answer, which is the kind that catches a wrong identification. **His age at death in 1924 will narrow the year first**, which is [row 124](/worklist/).

rows.what: Two Donato–Polistena marriages, a generation apart
rows.note: **The index turned up a second one and the archive only knew the first.** [Row 71](/worklist/) is about **Nunziata Donato × Giovanni Polistena**, about 1916. But the Scilla deaths also give **MARIA DONATO (d. 3 April 1911), «Padre Candeloro Donato, Madre Domenica Romano, Coniuge GIUSEPPE POLISTINA»** — a Donato woman married to a Polistena man a generation earlier. **Her father is a Candeloro Donato**, which is the name of both this archive's wall and Domenico Donato's son of 1847. **Two families that intermarried twice are usually close to begin with**, and the earlier act would say how.

rows.what: A second Generosa Costa at Scilla — guard the name before it merges
rows.note: **Rocco Arena's wife was Generosa Costa. So was Pasquale Donato's.** The death index gives **PASQUALE DONATO (d. 20 April 1937), «Padre Domenico, Madre Annunziata Sofi, Coniuge GENEROSA COSTA»** — and Pasquale is Michele Donato's brother, so this is inside the family, not a stranger who happens to share a name. **That is exactly the circumstance in which two women become one in a tree.** They are almost certainly different: Rocco's Generosa was born about 1868 and married in 1888. **Write the distinction down now**, while it is obvious, rather than discovering the merge later.

rows.what: Tell the estate that Antenati has a name index
rows.note: **This is not a Mazza finding, it is an estate finding, and the other archives are working Italian registers too.** `/search-nominative/?cognome=X&localita=Y&s_size=100` returns acts with **father, mother and spouse** already extracted, and for Scilla it covers deaths 1910–1943. **Falco and Defranceschi have been reading volumes the same way this archive has.** Worth a note carrying the query form, the `localita=` caution — `fq=` and `facets=` are **silently ignored** and return the unfiltered count — and the parsing rule that **only rows with a `p.morte` value are the deceased**; the rest are relatives seen from inside someone else's act, and reading them as deaths invents people.
